Treatment may include testosterone replacement and fertility treatment.

q: A patient presents with complaints of morning time productive cough that is yellow that increase on turning from left to right side. Which of the following lung diseases is likely to be present?

Explanation
A condition in which the lungs' airways become damaged, making it hard to clear mucus. Bronchiectasis may result from an infection or medical condition, such as pneumonia or cystic fibrosis. Mucus builds up and breeds bacteria, causing frequent infections. Symptoms include a daily cough that occurs over months or years and daily production of large amounts of phlegm. Treatment may include physiotherapy and medication, such as antibiotics and drugs to help loosen mucus.

q: A patient is identified as having tumor in ileum and leading to urinary 5hiaa being elevated. Diagnosis?

Explanation
A slow-growing cancerous tumour that can grow in several places throughout the body. A carcinoid tumour often begins in the stomach, appendix, small intestine, colon, rectum or lungs. Symptoms often don't appear until late in the disease and are vague. Examples include diarrhoea and skin flushing. Treatment includes surgery and medication, such as drugs that block cancer cells from secreting hormones or boost the immune system.

q: In an injury, it is noted under microscope that hair bulbs were crushed. Most likely the injury is:
e:
C. Lacerated wound
Explanation
tissues are torn as a result of application of blunt force.tissues may be skin,mucous membrane,muscles or internal organs. Laceration is 3 dimensional. General features of laceration: Irregular shape Irregular and uneven margins Contused edges Floor of laceration shows following features: Tissue bridges (tissue,blood vessels,and nerve bridging across the gap of the wound) Crushed Less haemorrhage because of crushed blood vessels Foreign particles like mud may be seen embedded in the wound,which gives clue about the scene of crime.

q: In court of law, examination of a witness is being is done to develop new & old facts & to try to weaken the evidence by showing that evidence was biased, inaccurate, inconsistent by lawyer during which of the following?

Explanation
Direct examination : Done by the Defence lawyer,in this Prior developed evidence like MLC,postmortem is submitted . Cross examination : done by the prosecutor to develop new or old facts . Leading questions are allowed only during cross examination.

q: A patient died because of doctor negligence but some other factors also were present for the reason of death. This kind of malpractice is known as
e:
B. Res ipsa loquitor
Explanation
When both the doctor negligence and other factors from patient are present it is contributory negligence. Novus actus interveniens : New intervening act leading to damage/loss/or death. Res ipsa loquitor is facts sufficient to prove negligence of doctor with no contributory negligence from patients.

q: A person was brought to opd with history of snake bite 8hrs ago. Patient was noted to be in respiratory depression & hr- 50 & drooping of eyelids was noted bilaterally. 10 vials antivenom was administered. In the hospital no ventilator was available. What is the next management?
e:
A. Give atropine + neostigmine
Explanation
The given symptoms of drooping of eyelids indicates neurotoxicity present. Neurotoxicity assessment is done for every 2 hours. The best management is pretreatment with atropine + neostigmine Blood coagulation profile not required as vasculotoxicity has been already ruled out. Hydrocortisone isused for serum sickness which presents 1-2 weeks later. and epinephrine given in anaphylactic reaction.

q: A 26 yr. old female presented with scaly skin. on histopathology neutrophils were diagnosis?
e:
C. Psoriasis
Explanation
A condition in which skin cells build up and form scales and itchy, dry patches. Psoriasis is thought to be an immune system problem. Triggers include infections, stress and cold. The most common symptom is a rash on the skin, but sometimes the rash involves the nails or joints. Treatment aims to remove scales and stop skin cells from growing so quickly. Topical ointments, light therapy and medication can offer relief.

q: What is the reason behind the antigenic shift in influenza virus?
e:
A. Mutation
Explanation
Human influenza A viruses evolve rapidly by antigenic shift and antigenic drift. Antigenic shift occurs by genetic reassortment between currently circulating human viruses and influenza viruses of other origin, by re-emergence of a previously circulating virus, and by invasion of animal influenza viruses .

q: Somatic antigen of O157:H7 is located on which part of bacterial cell?
